method: GitHub metadata, default-branch commit, README and retrievable license review; selected source/build/config files inspected. No Android integrations or performance benchmarks executed.

review.assessment: The richest symbolic conversation candidate: concepts, English rule parsing, topics, rejoinders and user facts. C++/JNI, serialized engine access, asset loading and script authoring are substantial work. English rule parsing is model-free; do not assume foreign TreeTagger assets or integrations meet the same constraints.

repositories.description: A RiveScript interpreter for Java. RiveScript is a scripting language for chatterbots.

review.decision: Prototype first as the simpler engine baseline
review.assessment: Java trigger/response scripting with variables, conditions and input/reply history. Suitable for small talk and personality packs. Old default-branch code, so own the maintenance risk; validate Android and R8. Not a general semantic interpreter or ready conversation corpus.

repositories.description: A RiveScript interpreter for JavaScript. RiveScript is a scripting language for chatterbots.

review.assessment: Same scripting family in JS. A useful reference for behavior or newer implementation choices; adds a JS runtime if embedded in native Run. Do not install both Java and JS engines.

repositories.description: Base content for AIML 2.0 chatbot

review.assessment: Ready AIML small-talk content, optimized for Pandorabots. A compatible local interpreter is required; platform extensions and personality need review. GPL content requires distribution-specific review for proprietary Run. Not a no-effort offline drop-in.

repositories.description: Python 3.x based AIML 2.0 Chatbot interpreter, framework, related programs and knowledge files

review.license_note: MIT-style license text; API reports NOASSERTION
review.assessment: AIML 2.1 interpreter and an extensive Python bot platform. Embedded Python use is documented, but the dependency list includes server/channel integrations and optional services. Interpreter license does not clear every bundled AIML file. Too much Android packaging work for its likely benefit.

repositories.description: State Transition Dialogue Manager
repositories.last_commit_message: Doc update for DialogueFlow transitions keyword arg

review.decision: Study its dialogue design; resolve license before copying
review.license_note: setup.py declares MIT; no root license retrieved
review.assessment: State-transition dialogue manager with Natex matching/generation, variables and macros. Strong example of mixed-initiative authored conversation. Python and NLTK/macros complicate Android and the no-model boundary; assess the exact enabled macros, not the project label.

repositories.description: A dialogue engine for creating chat bots

review.assessment: Scripted chatbot with topic/conversation facilities, but old JS stack and NLP dependencies need separate review. No demonstrated advantage over the simpler RiveScript baseline for Run.

repositories.description: Botkit is an open source developer tool for building chat bots, apps and custom integrations for major messaging platforms.

review.assessment: Archived server/channel bot framework. Helps connect bots to messaging platforms, not Run's offline understanding or local content. Does not supply the missing conversational intelligence.

repositories.description: 💬   Open source machine learning framework to automate text- and voice-based conversations: NLU, dialogue management, connect to Slack, Facebook, and more - Create chatbots and voice assistants

review.decision: Do not adopt under current constraints
review.assessment: Powerful intent/entity/dialogue framework, normally deployed with trained NLU/dialogue components in Python. Rule-only configurations exist, but adopting that stack does not provide a lightweight no-model Android solution.

repositories.description: ChatterBot is a machine learning, conversational dialog engine for creating chat bots

review.assessment: Learning/response-selection framework with a typical statistical NLP/training stack. Some adapters can be simple, but that is not an advantage over a controlled native retrieval layer. Evaluate its separately licensed corpus independently.

repositories.description: The open-source hub to build & deploy GPT/LLM Agents ⚡️
repositories.last_commit_message: fix(zai): extract parses valid JSON as-is before trying jsonrepair (3.1.2) (#15526)

review.license_note: MIT for inspected repository; services separate
review.assessment: Current AI-agent/platform ecosystem is centered on LLM/service integrations. Historical Botpress versions have different capabilities and licensing; they are not interchangeable evidence for a current offline solution.

repositories.description: modest natural-language processing

review.assessment: English tokenization, phrase matching and linguistic transformations without requiring a pretrained neural pipeline for its core rule/lexicon approach. Useful normalization reference. JS embedding/porting cost and linguistic mistakes remain; not a coreference or conversation engine.

repositories.description: An NLP library for building bots, with entity extraction, sentiment analysis, automatic language identify, and so more

review.decision: Do not adopt default NLU stack
review.assessment: Default intent manager trains a classifier. Model-free utilities could be isolated, but a full Node/NLU stack conflicts with the current no-trained-model constraint and adds unnecessary runtime complexity.

repositories.description: Developer friendly Natural Language Processing ✨

review.assessment: The documented pipeline loads a language model. Offline execution is not the same as model-free execution. Its tokenizer sibling can be evaluated independently.

repositories.description: Multilingual tokenizer that automatically tags each token with its type

review.assessment: Standalone rule-driven tokenizer. Potentially useful for punctuation, token boundaries and mentions, but requires JS or a port and does not solve dialogue state. Prefer native implementation if the gain is small.

repositories.description: Apache OpenNLP

review.decision: Do not adopt model-based NLP pipeline
review.assessment: Many useful language tasks require trained models. Some utility pieces may be model-free, but Java alone is not enough to satisfy Run's constraints or prove Android compatibility.

repositories.description: CoreNLP: A Java suite of core NLP tools for tokenization, sentence segmentation, NER, parsing, coreference, sentiment analysis, etc.
repositories.last_commit_message: Update version numbers in the README

review.assessment: Large NLP pipeline with trained resources and licensing/integration implications. Rule subcomponents do not justify packaging the full system for this app.

repositories.description: SymSpell: 1 million times faster spelling correction & fuzzy search through Symmetric Delete spelling correction algorithm

review.decision: Reuse algorithm or a reviewed JVM port
review.license_note: MIT code; frequency sources still need provenance
review.assessment: Fast typo correction and word segmentation based on dictionary deletes and frequency data. Helpful for misspelled commands. Original is C#, not a native Kotlin dependency. Never silently rewrite task titles, place names, dates or quantities.

repositories.description: A natural language date parser in Javascript

review.decision: Strong date-parser reference; optional JS prototype
review.assessment: Calendar/date ranges, reference dates and explicit versus inferred fields. More expressive than scattered date regexes, but JS integration and Run's date policies must be evaluated. Extracting a date does not say whether it belongs to travel, exam or a subtask.

repositories.description: python parser for human readable dates
repositories.last_commit_message: Parse Korean absolute dates written with 년/월/일/시/분 (#1434)

review.assessment: Broad multilingual date parsing in Python. Useful for generating examples and comparison data without deploying Python into Run. Its defaults still need explicit locale, relative-base and future/past policies.

repositories.description: Java natural language date parser
repositories.last_commit_message: enable auto release to maven central

review.assessment: Grammar-based natural-language dates on the JVM. A plausible model-free Java candidate, but very old default-branch code and date/time dependencies need review. Preserve timezone, ambiguous-date and calendar-validity checks around it.

repositories.description: Language, engine, and tooling for expressing, testing, and evaluating composable language rules on input strings.
repositories.last_commit_message: Remove Support Ukraine banner from Duckling README

review.decision: Corpus/rule reference only under strict no-model policy
review.license_note: BSD-style with PATENTS file; review exact terms
review.assessment: Excellent typed time/number/unit rule corpus, but the tree also contains generated ranking classifiers. Haskell/native packaging is substantial. Do not describe the default system as entirely model-free. Removing ranking would be a separate fork to prove.

repositories.description: Microsoft.Recognizers.Text provides recognition and resolution of numbers, units, date/time, etc. in multiple languages (ZH, EN, FR, ES, PT, DE, IT, TR, HI, NL. Partial support for JA, KO, AR, SV). Packages available at: https://www.nuget.org/profiles/Recognizers.Text, https://www.npmjs.com/~recognizers.text
repositories.last_commit_message: Remove unused NuGet.CommandLine dependency to fix CVE-2024-0057 (#3203)

review.assessment: Typed date/time, number, unit and related extraction through rule/resource recognizers. Java implementation exists but the README calls it in progress; .NET has primary feature coverage. Java POMs target 8 but include JVM dependencies. An API named Model does not itself imply trained ML weights.

repositories.description: ANTLR (ANother Tool for Language Recognition) is a powerful parser generator for reading, processing, executing, or translating structured text or binary files.
repositories.last_commit_message: - Typescript runtime: adding .js to to imports in d.ts files (#4826)

review.decision: Use only for a deliberately authored grammar
review.assessment: Mature parser generator/runtime useful for typed edit commands and compound syntax. It does not come with a complete conversational English grammar. Generated parser code is a runtime cost to evaluate against simpler Kotlin grammar tools.

repositories.description: Elegant parsing in Java and Scala - lightweight, easy-to-use, powerful.

review.decision: Alternative grammar library; not first choice
review.assessment: PEG/parser-combinator approach for composing grammar rules. Useful alternative to regex sprawl, but Java/Scala tooling and dependencies need review. Not dialogue understanding out of the box.

repositories.description: A Kotlin and Swift DSL for finite state machine

review.assessment: Contains Kotlin and Swift despite GitHub labeling the repository Swift. Explicit transitions and effects can help ownership. Smaller conceptual fit than a large conversation framework, but advanced history/persistence requirements remain app work.

repositories.description: A powerful Kotlin Multiplatform state machine library with clean DSL syntax and first-class Kotlin Coroutines support

review.assessment: Kotlin/Android support, guarded/nested states, history and optional event persistence. Core depends on Kotlin stdlib. Useful for pending questions, interruptions and resumption. Verify library/Kotlin version compatibility; Run uses Kotlin 2.0.21. State transitions alone do not interpret text.

repositories.description: State machines, statecharts, and actors for complex logic

review.decision: Architecture/reference; runtime only if JS is justified
review.assessment: Strong statecharts, actors and explicit event handling. Excellent reference for ownership and interruption design. Native Kotlin Run would otherwise acquire a JS runtime just for state management.

repositories.description: Apache Commons SCXML

review.assessment: Standard XML statecharts and Java execution. Fits explicit dialogue states conceptually, but XML/runtime expression dependencies can be more cumbersome than native Kotlin state management.

repositories.description: Apache Lucene open-source search software
repositories.last_commit_message: Open files twice for sequential reads only when it helps (#16883)

review.decision: Do not add current full runtime by default
review.assessment: Strong lexical retrieval and ranking, but inspected mainline build documentation asks for JDK 25. Neither Java branding nor an older release establishes Android support. Run already uses Room 2.6.1; evaluate a Room FTS4 curated-content index first. Android platform SQLite cannot universally be assumed to expose FTS5.

repositories.description: Code for building ConceptNet from raw data.

review.assessment: Concept relations can expand topic associations and suggest relevant follow-ups. Full graph/build stack is inappropriate for a phone. Data is noisy, does not establish a fact or task requirement, and requires source attribution. Exclude Numberbatch embeddings under no-model policy.

repositories.description: Please see the readme file as well as our 2019 EMNLP paper linked here -->

review.license_note: TM-1 through TM-4 READMEs state CC BY 4.0
review.assessment: Task-oriented dialogues with corrections and realistic user phrasing. Strong source for conversation scenarios and annotated slots. Not an executable assistant or broad knowledge base. Repository archived; static examples remain useful. Attribute adapted source examples.

repositories.description: The Schema-Guided Dialogue Dataset

review.decision: Priority reference for multi-domain state and repair
review.assessment: Annotated intents, slots, services and state transitions useful for interruption/clarification design. Do not import it as a response brain or assume training scripts fit no-model runtime. Adapted data retains relevant share-alike obligations.

repositories.description: Large datasets for conversational AI
repositories.last_commit_message: Add new line in references section (#63)

review.decision: Reference only; no bulk response import
review.license_note: Apache-2.0 tooling; each source dataset differs
review.assessment: Provides processing recipes for response-selection datasets, not a single uniformly licensed conversation pack. Reddit/subtitle-style data is noisy and often mismatched to a personal assistant. Do not inherit the code license onto source conversations.

repositories.description: Source code for end-to-end dialogue model from the MultiWOZ paper (Budzianowski et al. 2018, EMNLP)

review.decision: Use selected multi-domain examples for design/evaluation
review.license_note: MIT at repository root; verify exact dataset/version provenance
review.assessment: Useful reference for travel-like slot filling and cross-domain turns. Domains and annotations have limitations; it does not give a general-purpose travel planner or license live factual claims. Data-driven scenario work need not mean training a model.

repositories.description: Java implementation of algorithms from Russell And Norvig's "Artificial Intelligence - A Modern Approach"
repositories.last_commit_message: Documentation improved for new Java versions.

review.assessment: Classic logic/search/planning implementations for learning and prototyping. No pretrained model is required for symbolic algorithms, but it is not a production Android conversation engine. Do not import an educational framework wholesale.

repositories.description: An open-source Java library for Constraint Programming

review.assessment: Constraint programming can improve prerequisite, availability and resource scheduling after text is parsed into data. Current POM targets Java 17; Android/API/dependency behavior must still be proved. Avoid optional native continuous-solver features and bound solve time.

repositories.description: Midstream of https://github.com/apache/incubator-kie-optaplanner
repositories.last_commit_message: Update Node.js version to v22 in Jenkinsfile

review.assessment: Large planning/optimization framework. Useful modeling references, but footprint, lifecycle and runtime assumptions need review. It cannot interpret conversation or remember dialogue for Run.

repositories.description: The open source Solver AI for Java and Kotlin to optimize scheduling and routing. Solve the vehicle routing problem, employee rostering, task assignment, maintenance scheduling and other planning problems.

review.assessment: Modern scheduling/optimization tooling. README requires Java 21+, and community versus enterprise features differ. Desktop Java/Kotlin support is not Android support. No conversational benefit until structured constraints already exist.

repositories.description: A generic Java toolkit for building dialogue systems

review.assessment: Java dialogue manager with probabilistic rules, Bayesian state and optional learning. Useful blackboard/state concepts, but its probabilistic models, speech plugins and desktop tooling need separate constraint review. No blanket no-model or distribution approval.
Archived browser dialogue/state/blackboard system with Tracery generation. Good examples of separating state from reply text. Not a maintained Android conversation framework.

repositories.description: A multilingual dialog corpus

review.assessment: Separate, user-contributed YAML dialogue corpus. A curated subset can become authored rules without training ChatterBot. Inspect individual files/provenance and rewrite persona, factual claims and generic chains. Broad factual correctness and natural multi-turn context are not guaranteed.

repositories.description: A nice parser combinator library for Kotlin

review.assessment: Kotlin parser combinators for composing command/edit grammar into typed results. Can improve add/remove/rename/summary/quantity syntax. We still author grammar and resolve references against the actual dialogue frame; verify current Kotlin artifact compatibility.

repositories.description: Java port of  SymSpell: 1 million times faster through Symmetric Delete spelling correction algorithm
repositories.last_commit_message: fix getEditDeletes to make prefixLength working (#69)

review.assessment: Java port of SymSpell; POM targets Java 8. Better packaging candidate than original C# for Run, but dependencies, dictionaries, maintenance and R8 still need checking. Restrict corrections to command vocabulary/high-confidence suggestions.

repositories.description: Tracery: a story-grammar generation library for javascript

review.decision: Reuse constrained generation ideas; JS or native subset
review.assessment: Grammar-based text expansion with reusable bindings and variation, without an LLM. Helpful for varied acknowledgements/personality after a response intent is chosen. Does not understand input, maintain true memory or validate facts; do not make all variation random.
